pull_request.title: Preserve README bytes in release preparation
pull_request.body:
Release preparation currently parses and rewrites the package README dependency example. Preserve the README bytes from the saved source instead, and maintain examples during ordinary documentation work. The README remains in the exact release file set and receipt/recovery checks, so independent edits still require reconciliation.

Remove the adapter's renderer delegation and redundant preflight invocation. Replace the normalization fixture with byte-preservation coverage through preparation and substituted publication, including UTF-8, CRLF and a missing final newline; retire the obsolete parser grammar matrix. Canonical snapshot selection at the existing Shared revision `3bef3f2daec7f64f875397ed4d53d5b9e2e68a08` removes only the renderer payload: 81 explicit roots, 112 files, unchanged remaining payloads and tool pins. Add pending 0.46.1 notes without changing package versions, lockfiles or library code.

Closes #119.

Validation in the isolated Linux checkout:

- `cargo +1.99.0 test --locked --offline --example repo-tool`: 56 passed, including rollback, interruption recovery, receipt binding and README preservation. Git/release effects are substituted.
- `cargo +1.99.0 clippy --locked --offline --example repo-tool -- -D warnings` and focused `rustfmt --check`: passed.
- `bash scripts/ci/test-release-adapters.sh`: passed, substitutes only. The first attempt lacked the checkout YQ selection; the successful retry used the existing binary after matching catalog pins and authenticating its SHA-256 and version. No tools were downloaded. A whole-host admission attempt rejected the unmanaged selection; no whole-host qualification is claimed.
- `make shared-tooling-check`: all 112 payloads passed.
- Canonical Shared documentation-link checker: 111 references in the four changed documents passed. This one-off check adds no snapshot dependency.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

No full suite, installed runtime qualification, native macOS execution or live release was performed. Required hosted checks and owner review remain the integration gate. Earlier failed fixture/admission logs are retained locally under `target/consumer-adoptions-020/` in the Shared Tooling checkout.

issue.body:
## Current delivered-source acceptance

Delivered on main at `3f87ddc1a0c1616775b2114c42a4adee7376c9b1` (Shared 0.20.0). The [exact-source CI matrix](https://github.com/dragginzgame/shared-tooling/actions/runs/39019838115) is complete and successful: change-scope, lint/security, Linux, native macOS ARM and native macOS Intel. The README renderer and its producer fixture/dispatch are retired. Consumer retirement remains separate in Memory #119 / PR #122: https://github.com/dragginzgame/ic-memory/issues/119 and https://github.com/dragginzgame/ic-memory/pull/122. That PR is not merged; existing snapshots retain their recorded bytes.

Earlier failed/cancelled runs retain their actual outcomes; no release, merge or consumer acceptance is inferred.

---

## Historical preparation and proposal

Retire `scripts/ci/render-cargo-readme-version.pl` and its dedicated fixture/portable-suite dispatch. Shared has no production caller, but the expanded consumer trace found IC Memory's `repo_tool::release_readme` using a recorded copy. Treat removal as a consumer-facing hard cut, with no alias or fallback parser.

Reviewed Shared HEAD: 0620c7f04c682037b0ab8fd0730acef5ea93aed8, plus the pending working-tree cleanup. Memory HEAD 93463259a07295f50146beb57c36adab303d9a37 already contains the caller; its independently dirty checkout was inspected only. Memory's recorded Shared 0.15.0 snapshot at 3bef3f2daec7f64f875397ed4d53d5b9e2e68a08 includes the helper as an explicit entrypoint.

The consumer must retire automatic README-example rewriting before adopting a snapshot without this entrypoint. Documentation examples remain consumer-owned; keep saved-source release admission, manifests/lockfiles/changelogs, receipts, recovery and publication authority unchanged. A separate Memory issue will own that adaptation. Existing recorded snapshots are immutable and unaffected by the Shared deletion.

The source removal is prepared locally; no release, tag, commit or consumer adoption is claimed. The Shared command removal requires minor notes; v0.18.0 already exists, so the pending proposal is 0.19.0. The real VERSION file remains maintainer-owned.

Consumer retirement is tracked in [Memory #119 — Retire README version rendering](https://github.com/dragginzgame/ic-memory/issues/119).

issue.title: Retire README version rendering before the Shared tooling hard cut

repository.name: ic-memory
repository.description: Durable stable-memory allocation governance for Internet Computer canisters

issue.body:
Shared Tooling is retiring its README dependency-example version renderer in the pending minor hard cut ([Shared #260 — Retire the README dependency-example version renderer](https://github.com/dragginzgame/shared-tooling/issues/260)). The helper has no Shared production caller, but Memory does use its explicitly selected snapshot entrypoint.

Read-only evidence: Memory HEAD 93463259a07295f50146beb57c36adab303d9a37 contains `README_VERSION_RENDERER`, `Repository::release_readme` and the `surfaces` call which rewrites `crates/ic-memory/README.md` while constructing candidate metadata. The same path remains in the separately dirty working source. `.shared-tooling.snapshot` selects Shared 0.15.0 at 3bef3f2daec7f64f875397ed4d53d5b9e2e68a08, recording the renderer as an entrypoint and file. No Memory source, snapshot, package version, index or Git ref was changed.

Recommended cut before adopting the removal:

- Remove automated README dependency-example rewriting from the release adapter and retire its entrypoint through the normal reviewed snapshot refresh. Keep README examples maintained as documentation rather than requiring a partial TOML parser during release.
- Preserve saved-source admission and the exact intended metadata/receipt file set. If README remains in that set, project its original bytes rather than rewriting it. Adjust the prepared/finalized payload comparison and focused release fixtures consistently.
- Keep manifest/lock/changelog preparation, package qualification, rollback/recovery, and consumer-owned publication authority unchanged. Do not edit the existing immutable snapshot in place or add an alias/fallback for the removed Shared command.

Acceptance: the consumer adapter no longer calls the retired command; snapshot selection no longer requests it; focused source-bound prepare/check/resume/refusal fixtures pass on the selected graph, including README byte preservation. This is contributor tooling work, so it need not force a Memory library minor by itself. Existing pinned snapshots continue to work until reviewed adoption; this issue does not claim that Shared's local deletion or Memory adoption is delivered.

Closing this 0.46-based contribution as superseded by direct release delivery and resolving #119. No PR merge or integration branch change is needed.
